newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression moves slowly in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression moves slowly in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: The 10th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season moved slowly through the Gulf of Mexico on Sunday but was no immediate threat to land, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) the center of the depression was near latitude 25.3 north and longitude 93.8 west or about 390 miles (625 km) south-southwest of New Orleans.
It was moving east-northeast near six mph (10 kph) and was expected to maintain that track at a slightly faster pace during the next 24 hours, forecasters said.
Maximum sustained winds were 35 mph (55 kph) and could strengthen during the next day, forecasters said.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
The depression would be named Josephine if it strengthened into a tropical storm.
